verses.text: This na Jesus Christ’s family record: David’s son, Abraham’s son. Roots go way back, fam. 🌱
Abraham fathered Isaac. Isaac fathered Jacob. Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers. The family line dey roll, no cap. 🌳
Judah fathered Perez and Zerah through Tamar. Perez fathered Hezron; Hezron fathered Ram. Family tree dey branch out, abeg. 🌿
Ram fathered Amminadab. Amminadab fathered Nahshon. Nahshon fathered Salmon. Next name, next generation. 📜
Salmon fathered Boaz through Rahab. Boaz fathered Obed through Ruth. Obed fathered Jesse. Family tree still growing. ✨
Jesse fathered King David. David the king fathered Solomon through the woman who had been Uriah’s wife. 👑
Solomon fathered Rehoboam. Rehoboam fathered Abijah. Abijah fathered Asa. The line carries on. 🔁
Asa fathered Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat fathered Joram. Joram fathered Uzziah. Next names in the family chain. ⛓️
Uzziah fathered Jotham. Jotham fathered Ahaz. Ahaz fathered Hezekiah. One generation hands off to the next. 🙌
Hezekiah fathered Manasseh. Manasseh fathered Amon. Amon fathered Josiah. The family record keeps rolling. 📖
Josiah fathered Jechoniah and his brothers when the people were exiled to Babylon. A hard turn in the story. 🧳
After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah fathered Shealtiel; Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel. The line kept going after exile. 🌅
Zerubbabel fathered Abiud. Abiud fathered Eliakim. Eliakim fathered Azor. Another generation, another handoff. 📝
Azor fathered Zadok. Zadok fathered Achim. Achim fathered Eliud. The names keep moving down the line. ➡️
Eliud fathered Eleazar. Eleazar fathered Matthan. Matthan fathered Jacob. The family record rolls on. 📜
Jacob fathered Joseph, Mary’s husband. Mary gave birth to Jesus, who is called Christ. ✨
So, count it: Abraham to David—14 generations; David to the exile in Babylon—14; and the exile to Christ—14. Three sets, each fourteen. 🔢
Here’s how Jesus Christ was born: Mary was engaged to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, was a righteous man. He didn’t want to make her a public spectacle, so he planned to quietly break the engagement.

While Joseph was thinking it over, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will give birth to a son. Name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”
All this happened to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet:
“Look, the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son. They will call him Immanuel”—which means, “God with us.”
Joseph woke up and did what the Lord’s angel commanded him: he took Mary as his wife.
But he did not sleep with her until she gave birth to her firstborn son. Joseph named him Jesus.
Jesus was born in Bethlehem, Judea, during King Herod’s time. Then wise men from the east arrived in Jerusalem, asking, ✨
“Where is the child born King of the Jews? We saw his star out east and came to worship him.” 🌟
When King Herod heard this, he was troubled—and all Jerusalem with him.
He gathered the chief priests and scribes and asked them where the Christ was to be born.
They answered, “In Bethlehem of Judea. The prophet wrote this:
‘You, Bethlehem in Judah, are no small place among Judah’s princes; from you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”
Then Herod quietly called the wise men and got the exact time the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem and said, “Go search carefully for the child. When you find him, report back, so I can go worship him too.”
They heard the king and set out. The star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it stopped above the place where the child was. 🧭
When they saw the star, joy hit them big-time—overwhelming joy. 🌟
They entered the house and saw the child with Mary, his mother. They bowed down and worshiped him. Then they opened their treasures and offered him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh. 🎁
A dream warned them not to return to Herod, so they went back to their own country by another route.

After they left, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream: “Get up. Take the child and his mother and escape to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, because Herod is going to search for the child to kill him.”
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother by night, and left for Egypt. 🌙
He stayed there until Herod died. This fulfilled what the Lord had spoken through the prophet: “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

When Herod realized the wise men had outsmarted him, he flew into a rage. He ordered the killing of all the boys aged two and under in Bethlehem and the surrounding region, based on the exact time he had learned from the wise men.
Then what the prophet Jeremiah had spoken came to pass:
“A voice was heard in Ramah—crying, weeping, deep mourning. Rachel was weeping for her children; she would not be comforted, because they were gone.”
After Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream while he was in Egypt.
“Get up. Take the child and his mother and go to Israel, because those who were trying to take the child’s life are dead.”
Joseph got up, took the child and his mother, and returned to the land of Israel.
But when he heard Archelaus was ruling Judea in place of his father Herod, Joseph was afraid to go there. Warned in a dream, he went instead to the region of Galilee.
He settled in a city called Nazareth. This fulfilled what the prophets had spoken: “He will be called a Nazarene.” 🏡
Around that time, John the Baptizer showed up preaching in Judea’s wilderness. His message was:
“Repent—turn back! Heaven’s Kingdom is close.”
This is the one Isaiah the prophet was talking about: “A voice shouting in the wilderness: ‘Get the Lord’s road ready; make his paths straight!’”
John wore camel-hair clothes, with a leather belt around his waist. His food? Locusts and wild honey. That’s the menu. 🦗🍯
People came out to him from Jerusalem, all Judea, and the whole region around the Jordan.
They were baptized by John in the Jordan as they confessed their sins.
But when John saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, he said, “You brood of snakes! Who warned you to run from the coming wrath? 🐍
Then show fruit that proves you’ve repented!
Don’t tell yourselves, ‘Abraham is our father.’ I’m telling you: God can raise children for Abraham from these stones.
The ax is already at the roots of the trees. Every tree that produces no good fruit will be chopped down and thrown into the fire. 🪓🔥
“I baptize you in water for repentance. But the one coming after me is stronger than I am. I’m not even worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
His winnowing fork is in his hand. He will thoroughly clear his threshing floor, gather the wheat into his barn, and burn the chaff with fire that can’t be put out.”
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
John tried to stop him, saying, “I’m the one who needs to be baptized by you, and you’re coming to me?”
Jesus answered him, “Let it happen for now. This is the right way for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then John let him.
As soon as Jesus was baptized, he came straight up out of the water. Then the heavens opened, and he saw God’s Spirit coming down like a dove and resting on him. 🕊️
A voice from heaven said, “This is my dearly loved Son. I’m so pleased with him.”
Then the Spirit led Jesus into the wilderness, where the devil would test him.
After fasting forty days and forty nights, hunger hit him.
The tempter came and said, “If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become bread.”
Jesus replied, “Scripture says, ‘A person doesn’t live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from God’s mouth.’”
Then the devil took him to the holy city and stood him on the highest point of the temple.
He said, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down. Scripture says, ‘He will command his angels about you,’ and, ‘They will carry you in their hands so you don’t hit your foot on a stone.’”
Jesus answered, “Scripture also says, ‘Do not test the Lord your God.’”
Again the devil took him to a very high mountain and showed him all the world’s kingdoms and their glory.
He said, “I’ll give you all this if you fall down and worship me.”
Then Jesus said, “Get behind me, Satan! Scripture says, ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve only him.’”
Then the devil left him, and angels came and took care of him. 🕊️
When Jesus heard that John had been arrested, he withdrew to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum, by the sea in the regions of Zebulun and Naphtali.
This fulfilled what God had spoken through Isaiah the prophet:
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, by the sea, beyond the Jordan—Galilee of the Gentiles:
The people living in darkness have seen a great light; light has dawned on those living in the land and shadow of death.” ✨
From then on, Jesus began preaching: “Repent! Heaven’s Kingdom is near.”
As Jesus walked beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers—Simon, called Peter, and his brother Andrew—throwing a net into the sea. They were fishermen.
He said to them, “Come follow me, and I’ll turn you into fishers of people.”
Right away they left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there, he saw two more brothers: James, Zebedee’s son, and John his brother. They were in a boat with their father Zebedee, repairing their nets. Jesus called to them.
They immediately left the boat and their father, and followed Jesus.
Jesus went all around Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.

News about him spread through all Syria. People brought him everyone who was sick or suffering from different diseases and pains, people with demons, people with seizures, and paralyzed people. He healed them.
Huge crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and the land across the Jordan.
